correctness.rationale: Uppal's reduction leaves the geometric types A2 and A4 over F4; each has one geometric singularity and two or four exceptional curves, respectively, so Proposition 9.5 gives separability. In the characteristic-two double-plane model, each rational zero of the nonzero quadratic coefficient has a unique rational lift. Two such zeros suffice. The only remaining conic is the pair of conjugate lines, whose binary anisotropic form can be scaled and transformed to X²+XY+ωY² (the mixed term is nonzero and all trace-one constants are equivalent by an Artin–Schreier shift). Independently recomputed the binary evaluation rank outside its single rational zero: in different projective charts and a different coefficient basis, direct enumeration of every subset of the 20 rows found exactly the empty relation and the sum of all 20 rows. The kernel has dimension 11. The map H↦H²+QH has image in that kernel and its domain has dimension 12 with kernel {0,Q}, so its image is the full trace kernel. If no rational point lies above a point where Q≠0, all trace values equal one. Subtracting ωQ² puts the quartic in the kernel, and shifting W by H+βQ, with β²+β=ω, yields two distinct geometric factors. This contradicts geometric integrality. Any fiber where Q≠0 with trace zero has two rational points, smooth by the W derivative in the corresponding affine chart. The resulting theorem uses no enumeration of all RDP surfaces, and the bound is sharp by the cited F2 examples.
residual_risks: The all-types reduction is an imported theorem, not a conclusion of the rank certificate. Geometric integrality is indispensable to the trace argument.

evidence: Separability and the F2 counterexamples come from Uppal. The standard trace formula on a resolution Y gives #Y(Fq)=q²+q Tr(F on Pic)+1. For A4 the rank-four exceptional space is a permutation representation. Its exceptional chain has 1+q Tr(F on that space) rational points (split chain or reversed chain with just the central crossing fixed). On the complementary rank-four space the canonical class is fixed, so the trace is at least −2. Subtracting the exceptional points gives at least 8 smooth points over F4. For A2 the corresponding dimension bound only gives a lower bound of zero for smooth points at q=4.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The A4 subcase is a short application of a known theorem even though Uppal lists it as unresolved. The universal F4 result does not follow from this calculation; the A2 obstruction and uniform anisotropic double-plane statement still add mathematical content.

value.rationale: The proof removes the remaining field-size exception apart from the genuinely sharp F2 boundary in a published RDP point theorem. Its trace-kernel factorization also gives a structural result for arbitrary integral separable double planes with the specified conic, not a finite census of presentations of the surface types. The value does not depend on claiming A4 as an independently new subcase.
